ITEM.PTXT: Pressure fluctuations occur in the intake pipe due to the intermittent intake strokes. The effect that pressure fluctuations remaining in the intake pipe after the intake valve closes have on the next intake stroke is called the pulsation effect. When the pressure fluctuation remaining after the intake valve closes is synchronized with the next intake stroke, the pressure at valve opening becomes higher, so the intake air volume increases and torque can be increased.

To actively utilize this pulsation effect, the variable intake system switches the effective intake pipe length in 2 stages in accordance with the cycle of the pulsating flow that changes with engine speed, increasing torque across the entire range.

ENTRY.PTXT: Detects the throttle valve opening angle.
Switches the intake pipe length in 2 stages by opening and closing the ACIS valve.
Laser welded to the resin surge tank, it opens and closes the ACIS valve upon receiving signals from the engine control computer.
Sends a signal to the electric ACIS rotary solenoid at the appropriate timing based on the signals from the sensors.
